newsitem.title: USA: Grist Mill seeks efficiencies to boost profits.
newsitem.headline: Grist Mill seeks efficiencies to boost profits.

text.p: Grist Mill Co said Tuesday it is working to improve its operating efficiencies and boost its profitability.

Earlier, Grist Mill, which makes private label cereals and other food products, reported earnings for the second quarter ended November 30 of $0.07 a share, down from $0.11 a year ago. Revenues were $27.6 million, up from $21.5 million.

"The lower levels of profitability reflect a decline in contract manufacturing profit margins and a shift in the product mix of grocery sales to newer items with lower profitability," Glen Bolander, chief executive officer, said.
Contract manufacturing sales, whereby Grist Mill makes food products for another company, declined 16 percent from last year as its largest contract customer reduced orders.
Bolander said sales growth was fueled by new products such as ready to eat cereals, fruit filled cereal bars and crisp rice marshmallow bars.
"While the profitability of these products is currently below our other grocery products, we are working to improve our operating efficiencies," he added.
He said Grist Mill has seen good sales growth for its store brand grocery products. It introduced a line of low fat chewy granola bars that are expected to be widely accepted.

"While progress is being made on lowering our costs, our overall operating efficiencies have not improved at the rate we desire," Bolander added. "We are focused on these issues and expect to see gradual improvements in production efficiencies in future quarters."

Bolander added the store-brand grocery business continues to be the primary focus of the company, with sales growing 45 percent over the prior year. This reflects its ready-to-eat cereal busines, up 67 percent thus far this year, and its wholesome snack bar businesses, up 66 percent.
